predecessors.name: Duchy of Cieszyn
predecessors.text: the Lesser Polish lands east of the Biała river, with the lands from which Zator and Toszek were created in 1445

ledger.x: c. 1315: Oświęcim splits from Cieszyn. 'It was established about 1315 on the Lesser Polish lands east of the Biała river'; 'the lands of Oświęcim east of the Biała were split off from [Cieszyn] as a separate duchy'.
1445: 'the duchies of Zator and Toszek were created from some the lands of the duchy'.

1457: the last duke, Jan IV, 'sold his duchy to King Casimir for the price of 3,000,000 Prague groschen' three years after declaring himself a vassal of Poland in 1454 ('re-united with Poland in 1454').
1457: the Duchy of Oświęcim ends; 'At the General sejm of 1564, King Sigismund II Augustus issued privileges of incorporation' into the Kraków Voivodeship.

certainty.note: The page names towns and the Biała river, not a boundary.
